annotation.method: Codex freshly read the complete 17-page paper in physical-PDF order, surveyed every proved or justified mathematical claim, and compared all candidates with the frozen Mathlib and importable NumStability baselines.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P31 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 2.3, monotonicity of the block 1-norm power-method estimates
rejected_candidates.reason: The proof is a short exact sign-duality, Hölder, and row-selection argument. Compiled NumStability supplies only generic norm notation for it, with the key power-method theorems remaining uncompiled; Mathlib and elementary finite-sum reasoning suffice. It therefore gives no T1/T2 advantage and is below the T3 difficulty floor.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the at-most n/t+1 termination statement for Algorithm 2.4
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper gives only the elementary counting reason that t new vertices are visited after each first iteration. A faithful relational statement is a short pigeonhole/counting consequence; encoding every imperative branch would add artificial program-verification difficulty not present in the source argument.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the exact iteration formulas for the worst-case family A_n(alpha)
rejected_candidates.reason: The formulas are stated with only 'straightforward to show' and no detailed proof. A full proof of every loop branch would require reconstruction not supplied as source proof text, while isolated geometric-series identities are too easy for T3.

The paper presents the estimator and explains its control flow but does not give a separate full correctness proof beyond the short monotonicity lemma. The frozen source tree has related Hager/Higham power-method correctness theorems, but their modules are absent from the importable L bundle.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithm 4.1 and the Schur-factorization resolvent representation
rejected_candidates.reason: Equations (4.1)-(4.2) and the per-grid-point cost discussion are standard exact matrix algebra and algorithmic accounting. The pseudospectral accuracy conclusions are empirical, and the closer resolvent modules in NumStability are uncompiled.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Examples 2.5 and the experiments in Sections 3-4
rejected_candidates.reason: These are particular numerical executions, performance tables, and contour-plot observations rather than difficult universally quantified theorems proved in the paper.

T1.decision: Skipped. No source-proved exact result needs one substantial compiled NumStability theorem. The compiled floating-point matrix-vector bounds address a different question, and the matching 1-norm power-method developments are unavailable source-only modules.

T2.decision: Skipped. No source proof needs at least two distinct substantial results from the frozen importable library. The paper does not analyze floating-point errors of its matrix products or triangular solves.

T3.decision: Skipped. Lemma 2.3 and the termination count are materially below qualifying-T2 difficulty. The worst-case loop formulas lack a detailed source proof, and expanding the algorithms' control flow solely to make a hard target would manufacture difficulty absent from the paper.

selection_policy: Use exact mathematical claims proved or justified in the paper, not empirical accuracy or timing observations.
Do not turn floating-point error theorems into dependencies for an exact-arithmetic paper proof.
Treat NumStability source-only power-method and pseudospectral modules as unavailable to condition L.
Do not inflate a short selection or counting argument by formalizing irrelevant imperative control-flow details.
Do not supply a detailed proof for a worst-case example when the paper merely asserts that its formulas are straightforward.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
